key_provisions_or_claims: Smart robots may be classed as things under Jordanian Civil Code Art. 291 (guardian liability) or as products under consumer protection and standards law.
Autonomy of smart robots strains guardianship liability because the custodian's control is uncertain.
Defective-product liability requires a defect, which fits poorly with harm from autonomous operation of non-defective robots.
Jordanian law lacks a definition of AI or smart robots.
Calls for modern, clear legislation to define responsibilities and protect rights.
annotation.summary_en: Jordanian doctrinal legal article examining whether smart robots are 'things' under guardian liability (Civil Code Art. 291) or 'products' under defective-product liability, drawing on French law. It finds both regimes inadequate for autonomous robots and calls for dedicated modern legislation.
annotation.title_clean: The Problem of Establishing Civil Liability for Harmful Effects of Smart Robots
annotation.title_en: The Problem of Establishing Civil Liability for Harmful Effects of Smart Robots
